title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Window a Block Purchase Reads Drawn Hours Over
content:
*Over what period are the hours drawn read?*

Where the tier lets unused hours roll into the next program year and the program has run less than a
full term, the hours drawn are read over the tier's block expiry period. Where the tier lets no unused
hours roll over, the hours drawn are read from the day the current term started, counting each month or
part month up to the day of the purchase. In any other case neither term above changes the window the
hours drawn are read over.

*Which figures of the Demand Service Rate Programs do those terms turn on?*

| Program | Unused hours roll into the next program year | Expiry period (calendar months) | Term (calendar months) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | No | 0 | 12 |
| Priority Response Program | No | 0 | 12 |
| Block Hour Service Program | Yes | 12 | 12 |
| Emergency Response Program | Yes | 12 | 12 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | Yes | 18 | 24 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | Yes | 24 | 24 |

*The terms in combination.*

| The program's rollover term | Months run since the current term started | The window read |
|---|---|---|
| unused hours roll over | fewer than the tier's term length | the tier's block expiry period |
| unused hours roll over | the tier's term length or more | neither term above changes the window |
| unused hours do not roll over | any | from the day the current term started to the day of the purchase, each month or part month counted |

*An illustration.* On the Dedicated Technician Program, where unused hours roll over, the expiry period
is 24 calendar months and the term is 24 calendar months, a program 9 months into its term reads the
hours drawn over 24 months. On the Priority Response Program, where unused hours do not roll over, the
hours drawn on a program 9 months into its term are read from the term start, which is 10 months
counting the part month up to the day of the purchase.
